court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: The lessee of three upper floors of a building rented out parts of the premises as furnished rooms by the week to various occupants, including the plaintiff's decedent, notwithstanding a covenant against housekeeping which the owner tacitly permitted to be violated. The court held that a subtenant of furnished rooms by the week acquired no easement over the roof as an appurtenance to her lease, and that permitted housekeeping use did not create one; her presence on the roof was that of a mere licensee. On that basis the judgment for the plaintiff-administrator was reversed and the complaint dismissed.

quotes.text: The lessee Haas rented out parts of the leased premises as furnished rooms to various people.
Plaintiff, his wife and child occupied two rooms on the top floor, hired by the week.

The plaintiff as a subtenant by the week of two furnished rooms had no easement over this roof as an appurtenance to his lease, and the mere fact that his immediate landlord, in violation of the principal lease, even with the acquiescence of the owner, permitted housekeeping in these furnished rooms, did not create an easement over the roof.

The plaintiff as a subtenant by the week of two furnished rooms had no easement over this roof as an appurtenance to his lease, and the mere fact that his immediate landlord, in violation of the principal lease, even with the acquiescence of the owner, permitted housekeeping in these furnished rooms, did not create an easement over the roof.

notes: Core holding is a premises-liability/licensee ruling, but facts and characterization of the weekly furnished-room subtenancy are directly on point and treated as an unremarkable, lawful arrangement.
